historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (12.8% 3yr / 15.3% 5yr) is more than 30% below EPS CAGR (21.1% / 26.3%) and the 5yr revenue CAGR (21.1%). The 5-year figures start from the COVID trough (FY2021) and FY2023 equity includes the share issue for Suzuki Motor Gujarat, so all of them overstate trend. The base path uses 17% for FY2027 (H1 actual +31%) then 8-9% decelerating to 5.5%, deliberately below every trailing CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF throughout (no SBC; investment income already outside OCF). FCF is erratic (FY2022 -16bn, FY2023 27bn, FY2026 87bn) because capex has tripled since FY2021 and working capital swings; FCF CAGRs are not a usable growth anchor.

scenario_narratives.base: Volumes fill the 2.9m-unit capacity in FY2027 (H1 revenue +31% on the GST 2.0 small-car revival) and then track capacity additions toward ~3.7m units by FY2031, with pricing and SUV mix adding 2-3% a year. The commodity/FX squeeze tied to the West Asia conflict eases gradually rather than snapping back: EBITDA margin (ex other income) recovers from 9.0% in FY2027 to an 11.5% mid-cycle level by FY2031, below the FY2024-25 peak because new SUV/EV models and higher depreciation dilute it. The INR 775bn capex plan is spent in full, so free cash flow is near zero in FY2027 and only normalises to ~5-6% of revenue once capex falls back toward depreciation. Maruti holds ~40% share; exports stay ~18-20% of volume.
scenario_narratives.bull: The margin compression proves purely cyclical: commodity and rupee headwinds reverse, operating leverage on the new Kharkhoda and Hansalpur lines comes through, and EBITDA margin returns to the FY2024-25 level of ~13.5% by FY2031. The seven-SUV launch programme closes the gap to Tata and Mahindra, small cars keep growing post-GST cut, and exports (Europe, Japan, Toyota OE supply) compound faster than domestic, taking revenue growth to 10-11% through FY2031 as the Khoraj plant fills.
scenario_narratives.bear: The squeeze is structural, not cyclical: Maruti keeps absorbing input costs to defend small-car affordability while Tata, Mahindra and Hyundai take SUV and EV share, and the GST-driven demand pull-forward fades after FY2027 (or a weak monsoon / policy reversal hits entry-level buyers). Revenue growth drops to 3-6%, EBITDA margin settles at 9.5% - near the FY2020 level and above the FY2021-22 trough - while the committed capex programme still has to be funded on a smaller revenue base, leaving new capacity under-utilised and depreciation heavier.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Maruti as two things: an operating franchise valued on mid-cycle margins after a fully-funded capex programme, and a liquid fund portfolio added at value less embedded tax and working cash. Neither FY2026's INR 87bn of free cash flow nor the FY2024-25 13% EBITDA margin is extrapolated - the first predates the capex ramp, the second predates the cost squeeze - and equally the 8.7% H1 FY2027 margin is not capitalised as permanent. Risk is carried in the scenario flows and the weights, with one INR-built discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle EBITDA margin is the dominant driver: each 1pp on the mature margin moves base value by roughly 8-10%
Capex of INR 775bn may not earn its cost of capital if SUV/EV share is not won; the bear case carries the spend on a smaller revenue base
The fund portfolio is ~30% of base intrinsic value; Suzuki (58.5%) controls its deployment, and minorities have no path to a distribution beyond the ordinary dividend

Indian equities trade on structurally higher multiples than an 11.5% INR discount rate with a 15x terminal cap supports; the gap between this value and the market price is largely a discount-rate disagreement, not an earnings one
GST policy, monsoon and commodity/FX are exogenous and can move a single year's margin by 3-4pp

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 10,985-17,370
data_sources.financials: MARUTI.NS_Metrics.csv and kpis table (FY2016-FY2026, quarters to Q2 FY2027); FY2026 Annual Report (notes 6.6, 22, cash flow statement); Q2 FY2027 standalone results, balance sheet and cash flow at 30 Sep 2026 (MARUTI.NS_Quarterly_Q2-2027.txt)
data_sources.qualitative: MARUTI.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): capex plan, capacity targets, margin commentary, competitive position

inputs.share_count_basis: 314.40m shares of INR 5 (paid-up capital INR 1,572m / 5), unchanged since the FY2023 preferential issue to Suzuki for Suzuki Motor Gujarat. Basic = diluted (EPS identical in every period); no options, convertibles or SBC, so the count is held flat.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income INR 3,839m plus INR 37,406m of debt-mutual-fund gains are NOT inside reported FCF: Ind AS cash flow statements back them out of operating cash flow (interest received and fund proceeds sit in investing), and the EBITDA series used for the margin path excludes Other income. Nothing further to strip; the matching asset (the fund portfolio) is in the bridge at value.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment: Maruti has no ESOP/RSU scheme and no SBC line in any FY2016-FY2026 cash flow statement (SBC-zero market; explicit 0% row kept).
inputs.cash_composition: Standalone balance sheet 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY2027 results): non-current investments 655,379 + current investments 43,390 + cash and equivalents 8,817 + other bank balances 5,140 = 712,726. Roughly INR 664bn of this is debt mutual funds (FY2026 AR: 717,238 at 31 Mar 2026, rolled forward for H1 net redemptions of ~74bn and ~20bn of gains); ~35bn is associates/subsidiaries at cost and quoted equity at FVTOCI; ~14bn cash and deposits. The interim does not split the investment line, so the whole reported figure is used and the haircuts are taken in equity_bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built: 10-year G-sec yield ~6.5-7% plus ~6.5% India equity risk premium at beta ~0.75 (zero debt, market leader, cyclical consumer durable) = ~11.5% cost of equity; no borrowings so WACC = cost of equity. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, share loss and margin risk are charged in the flows and weights, not stacked in the rate. Terminal growth 5.0% is INR nominal (~4% inflation target + ~1% real), well below India's ~10% nominal GDP growth.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A (leases as debt): lease liabilities of INR 830m (434 non-current + 396 current, 30 Sep 2026) are the whole of total_debt; lease cash (~INR 0.4bn/yr) is immaterial and not deducted from flows. The INR 40.1bn 'acquisition of right-of-use asset' in H1 FY2027 is an upfront leasehold land payment (new site), treated as capex in the FY2027 capex ratio.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial. Flows are built on the standalone entity, which after the Suzuki Motor Gujarat amalgamation (appointed date 1 Apr 2025) is >99% of the group; subsidiaries/associates are carried inside the investment line at cost.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (INR WACC, SBC-zero, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). Reason: automotive OEM whose value is an operating cash-flow stream plus a very large non-operating fund portfolio; not a financial, REIT or holdco. SETUP: this is a peak-volume / trough-margin moment with a capex supercycle on top. H1 FY2027 EBITDA margin (ex other income) was 8.7% against 11.7% in FY2026, 13.2% in FY2025 and an FY2016-FY2026 average of ~11.9%; H1 FY2027 free cash flow was about -INR 32bn (OCF 54.7bn less 86.5bn capex including land). The build therefore does not extrapolate FY2026 FCF (INR 87bn): year 1 is close to zero FCF and margins recover only to an 11.5% mid-cycle level in base. CAPEX: INR 775bn guided FY2027-FY2031 is modelled explicitly (base first-five-year capex sums to ~INR 765bn). CASH: the fund portfolio is ~17% of market cap and is added at reported value less employee-welfare funds, deferred tax on unrealised gains and an operating liquidity buffer. KNOWN SMALL DOUBLE COUNT (conservative): the balance sheet is 30 Sep 2026 but the FY2027 flow is the full year, so the H1 FY2027 cash burn of ~INR 32bn (~INR 100/share) is charged twice. No buybacks have ever been made; flat share count is factual, not a convention. House and street bases coincide (no SBC): band collapsed, band_position null.

base.ebitda_margin_note: EBITDA excludes Other income. FY2027 9.0% = H1 actual 8.7% with a modest H2 recovery; mid-cycle 11.5% sits just under the 11-year average (11.9%) and well under the FY2024-25 level (13.1-13.2%).
base.capex_note: First five years sum to ~INR 765bn against the INR 775bn FY2027-31 plan; FY2027 includes the INR 40bn land payment. Terminal 4.0% vs D&A 3.6%.
base.wc_note: Negative working capital (payables exceed inventory plus receivables), so growth releases cash: FY2024 and FY2026 released ~7% of incremental revenue, FY2025 ~0%. 2% taken.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the house 15% to 25%: margin compression is live and worsening on the latest print (Q2 FY2027 net profit -27% YoY), and Maruti lags in the two fastest-growing segments (SUV, EV) while committing to its largest ever capex programme. Base 50%: gradual recovery to a mid-cycle margin is what the 11-year record supports. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs commodity/FX reversal, SUV share gains and full utilisation of ~1m units of new capacity all at once. No solvency risk in any scenario (zero debt, ~INR 700bn of liquid funds).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
